body.estimand_functional: \(\theta(P)=\mathbb E_{P_X}[\tau_P(X)_+-\pi_0(X)\tau_P(X)]\), with frontier \(W_{T,\delta}(\rho;\mathcal Q)=\inf_{\mathsf D\in\mathfrak D_T(\rho;\mathcal Q)}\inf_{I_T\in\mathfrak C_{T,\delta}(\mathsf D;\mathcal Q)}\sup_{P\in\mathcal Q}\mathbb E_{P,\mathsf D}|I_T(O_{1:T})|\)

sampling_model.design: One \(P\)-independent non-anticipating contextual design chooses the known propensity \(e_t^{\mathsf D}(H_{t-1},X_t)\) from observed history and the fresh context; one \(P\)-independent Borel interval map is evaluated on the resulting observed trajectory.
sampling_model.units: The contexts are independent draws from a stationary density on \([0,1]^d\); the observed reward satisfies \(Y_t=\mu_{A_t}(X_t)+\sigma\varepsilon_t\) with fresh conditionally independent standard-normal innovations.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment satisfies \(A_t\mid(H_{t-1},X_t)\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(e_t^{\mathsf D})\), and only the selected-arm reward \(Y_t\) is observed.
sampling_model.overlap: No exogenous propensity floor is imposed; the design must generate any exploration needed for honesty while satisfying \(\sup_P\mathcal R_T(P,\mathsf D)\le\rho\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No attaining nuisance estimator is currently part of the core. The corrected object is an occupation-measure relaxation. Any upper theorem must explicitly construct predictable regression or approximation estimates, interval endpoints, bias control, and coverage from the realized adaptive sample.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1, 2, 5, and 6 give and attain a Pareto product frontier between participant regret and treatment-effect point-estimation error in a finite-armed experiment.
Theorem 5.1 gives the minimax regret exponent under the local Hölder--margin condition, and Proposition 3.1 yields \(\alpha\beta\le d\) for finite \(\alpha\).
The local asymptotic minimax result bounds regular ATE estimation under every covariate- and history-dependent assignment design.
Theorem 1 characterizes pathwise differentiability of the optimal value and Theorem 2 gives online one-step inference under a negligible rule-value remainder.
The paper derives minimax rates for nonsmooth \(L_r\)-functionals by polynomial approximation and moment-matching priors in fixed Gaussian white noise.
The lower and upper results match a CATE mean-squared-error versus regret frontier for finitely many contexts with fixed-order gaps.
The central theorem gives a studentized central limit theorem for predictably weighted augmented inverse-propensity estimators of fixed arm values.
The CADR theorem obtains asymptotic normality for a fixed contextual-policy value by conditional-variance stabilization.
Theorem 1 constructs nonasymptotic doubly robust confidence sequences for a fixed off-policy value under predictable logging policies.

The paper constructs one-sided lower confidence bands for optimal welfare that remain valid regardless of the margin condition; uniform separation and margin behavior govern its first-order welfare--precision comparison.
The main theorem derives asymptotic normality and adaptive semiparametric efficiency for regular scalar targets under directional stability and verifies the condition for LinUCB.

Section 4.1, Theorem 1 proves stability and asymptotic normality for ordinary least squares under regularized EXP4, yielding asymptotically exact Wald intervals for fixed linear functionals; Section 4.2, Theorem 2 gives the same algorithm a near-minimax regret bound.

body.tldr: An adaptive experiment that protects current participants suppresses observations from inferior treatments, while honest inference on the gain from individualized targeting needs those observations and is nonregular near treatment ties. The proved results establish class nonemptiness, the published feasibility rate after a predictable Gaussian-martingale transfer, an all-procedure coverage-to-information converse, and, for sufficiently large horizons in its displayed budget range, the fixed-gap \(\rho^{-1/2}\) frontier. The corrected general construction is a baseline-indexed occupation-measure relaxation: it includes every same-context-law, off-cell-agreeing target-separating alternative, uses exact pointwise Gaussian information, and enforces stochastic context capacity and participant welfare. Every narrow honest procedure must satisfy this relaxation, and its Lagrange lower value obeys weak duality. Saturation, strong duality, an explicit H\"older-local rate, and realization of the baseline-specific profiles by one law-independent adaptive design and connected interval remain open; the \(d=1\), \(\beta=1\), \(\alpha=1/5\), \(\rho\asymp T^{3/5}\) case remains the mandatory early kill test.

project_justification.gap: Existing regret--inference Pareto results treat point-estimation error in finite-arm, finite-feature, or finitely stratified models, while adaptive confidence-interval results generally take logging propensities as given and optimal-value inference does not price exploration by participant welfare. None combines a common observed-trajectory interval, nonregular positive-part geometry, continuous-context arrival capacity, and a hard uniform welfare budget. The remaining gap is not a missing scalar allocation formula: it is saturation and common sequential realization of baseline-indexed occupation profiles.
project_justification.niche: The targeting gain \(\mathbb E[\tau_+-\pi_0\tau]\) combines a regular benchmark term with a nonsmooth positive-part term. A welfare budget makes information endogenous because an arm's local information is integrated against a context-dependent occupation measure while its cost is the baseline gap. This produces a baseline-indexed sequential modulus with stochastic context-capacity constraints.
project_justification.fill: The procedure-free coverage theorem converts target separation and adaptive Gaussian information into a lower bound for every design and interval. The corrected local sets include all same-context-law alternatives agreeing off a cell whose target separation exceeds \(2w/(1-2\delta)\), without a sign-switch restriction. Arm-specific occupation measures yield the exact information integral; the global relaxation enforces context-arrival domination and welfare cost before taking the worst baseline. Its Lagrange lower value obeys proved weak duality, and every honest width-\(w\) procedure induces a feasible occupation profile, giving \(W_{T,\delta}\ge w_{T,\rho}\). The open kernel is to evaluate and saturate this implicit width and to realize its baseline-specific profiles by one predictable design and connected honest interval.

body.related_work: Perchet and Rigollet supply the cited H\"older--margin regret exponent used only for the feasibility boundary. Simchi-Levi and Wang establish a finite-arm regret--estimation frontier, and Li, Shi, and Simchi-Levi balance regret and CATE error over finitely many contexts; neither resolves continuous-context honest width under a hard welfare budget. Hu, Kallus, and Mao motivate selective local exploration, while Hadad and coauthors, Bibaut and coauthors, Waudby-Smith and coauthors, Cook, Mishler, and Ramdas, and Shen and coauthors provide adaptive-score or stability tools when the logging design or regular target is supplied. Luedtke and van der Laan and Ponomarev and Semenova address nonregular optimal-welfare inference without optimizing welfare-constrained data collection. Kaufmann, Capp\'e, and Garivier support the adaptive Gaussian change-of-measure step, and Cai and Low support the coverage-to-length logic. None of these sources proves saturation, strong duality, or law-independent sequential realization for the corrected baseline-indexed occupation relaxation; those claims remain open rather than being imported from prior work.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The occupation program is a necessary baselinewise relaxation, not an estimator. Its inner optimizer may depend on the unknown baseline law, and separate feasible profiles need not be compatible with one predictable law-independent design. Monotonicity alone does not control a jump at \(w_{T,\rho}\), and weak duality alone does not yield strong duality or attainment. The bump lemma and regret packing do not by themselves evaluate the scalar targeting-gain width because target contributions can cancel and adaptive allocation can concentrate on selected contexts.
body.honest_scope: The established scope consists of class nonemptiness, the cited feasibility exponent with its predictable Gaussian-martingale transfer, the all-design coverage--information converse, the fixed-gap \(\rho^{-1/2}\) theorem for sufficiently large horizons in its displayed budget range, the target-separating bump construction, weak duality for the corrected occupation relaxation, and the necessary bounds \(\Omega_{T,\delta}\ge2w_{T,\rho}/(1-2\delta)\) and \(W_{T,\delta}\ge w_{T,\rho}\). The width and modulus equal \(+\infty\) when the uniformly feasible design class is empty. The exact H\"older-local rate, saturation and right-regularity of \(\mathcal B_{T,\rho}\), strong duality or attainment, and realization by one predictable design and connected interval remain answer-open. At \(\rho\asymp T\), a completed result must recover fixed-design honest inference; on the fixed-gap subclass and for sufficiently large horizons it recovers \(\rho^{-1/2}\); below \(T^{r_{\beta,\alpha,d}}\), the design class is empty.
